title: Research: nonlinear messages keep the A7+A1 nine-term COPY floor at 72 (no new kappa)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Matarener"} -->
_Requested by **Mark**_

**Scoped negative result; no new κ.**

Before: [a7-a1-decoder-floor](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/main/research/a7-a1-decoder-floor) (#1224 frame) proves the separate-term COPY floor 72 for every complex shift, but only for linear messages. Its scope list puts arbitrary nonlinear decoder architectures outside the theorem.

After: on the same fixed nine-term supports, every deterministic zero-error nonlinear message (AND gates allowed) priced by its width still costs at least 72. That holds for every shift without reader side information. On both pinned sharp witnesses it also holds when readers know every orthogonal input.

How: Lemma 1 uses a fooling block, an invertible `B[S,R]` of size `rho_k` per term, so any message needs `2^rho_k` values. Lemma 2 turns side information into index coding on the induced orthogonality graph of each term's demand. The checker finds an induced Petersen + (rho_k − 5) isolated-line witness (rate rho_k; the rho=9 case is the 14-vertex witness of `p112-characteristic-two-minrank`) or a rho_k-line non-orthogonal set in every term of the `(0,9^8)` and `(1,8,9^7)` witnesses. Both totals are 72.

New package: `research/a7-a1-nonlinear-copy-floor` (base `ff3cc58e3`, card `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, scope changed). It uses the standard library only and runs in about 2 s.

```text
PASS_A7_A1_NONLINEAR_COPY_FLOOR roots=120 witnesses=2 no_side_info=72 orthogonal_side_info=72 petersen_terms=16 certificate=09a3e17032f727cb no_new_kappa
PASS_A7_A1_NONLINEAR_COPY_FLOOR_CONTROLS rejected=9
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/a7-a1-nonlinear-copy-floor outcome=negative-result
```

Limits: other architectures, shared COPY billing and receivers that combine terms nonlinearly are not covered. The side-information floor for *every* shift is left open in the package's open questions. With side information even linear codes can drop below a term's rank on small demand graphs, so that question is a contract change and not a nonlinear effect. The frozen predecessor is unchanged.
